extracted.intended_audience: Federal Trade Commission, Department of Justice, and federal agencies conducting regulatory reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for federal agencies (and the FTC/DOJ) on how to identify, assess, prioritize, and recommend repeal or modification of anticompetitive regulations under the April 9, 2025 Executive Order. Recommends use of the OECD Competition Assessment Toolkit and application of an econometric ACMD model to assemble a consolidated list for OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: OECD Competition Assessment Toolkit — competition checklist (four principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Toolkit’s checklist provides four principles for identifying anticompetitive regulations, focusing on provisions that (1) limit the number or range of suppliers; (2) limit the ability of suppliers to compete; (3) reduce the incentives of suppliers to compete; and (4) limit the choices and information available to consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toolkit Volume 1 sets forth these principles and a detailed analytical methodology for evaluating regulations that raise anticompetitive concerns. The checklist is the central screening device for identifying provisions that unduly restrict competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply Toolkit analytical methodology and implementation procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Toolkit includes three volumes: principles and checklist (volume 1), detailed technical guidance on key issues (volume 2), and an operational manual with a step-by-step process (volume 3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the full Toolkit process — screening with the checklist, applying technical considerations, and following the operational/manual steps — when performing competition assessments. OECD country experiences (e.g., Canada, South Korea, Mexico, Tunisia) illustrate practical application. Agencies may need to adapt Toolkit procedures to specific agency contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a transparent process with screening devices (OECD Council Recommendation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Governments should introduce an appropriate process to identify existing or proposed public policies that unduly restrict competition and develop specific and transparent criteria for competition assessment, including the preparation of screening devices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendation also urges an appropriate process for revision of existing or proposed public policies that unduly restrict competition and for developing specific/transparent criteria to evaluate suitable alternatives. Agencies should adopt explicit screening criteria and revision mechanisms as part of regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order Section 3(e) requirement — consolidated list for OMB
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3(e) of the White House Executive Order directs the FTC, in consultation with the White House, the DOJ, and federal agencies, to provide OMB with 'a consolidated list of regulations that warrant rescission or modification in light of their anti-competitive effects, along with recommended modifications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidated list should identify candidate regulations for repeal or modification and include recommended textual or regulatory changes. Assessment tools and models (e.g., Toolkit, econometric models) should feed into prioritization for the list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use econometric SRB-Œ≥ model to evaluate ACMDs' economic impact
rubrics_metrics.description: An econometric framework (the SRB-Œ≥ model) was developed to analyze anticompetitive market distortions (ACMDs) and their impact on GDP per capita, grounded on the notion that a competitive, high-growth economy relies on three pillars: property rights protection, domestic competition, and international competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the econometric model to quantify the economic cost of ACMDs and to prioritize regulations for rescission or modification. The model can help assemble and rank the consolidated list submitted to OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property rights protection as an evaluation pillar
rubrics_metrics.description: Property Rights Protection: A well-functioning economy depends on strong property rights. When rights to land, intellectual property, or assets are insecure, investment declines and incentives to innovate fall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess regulations for their effects on security of property rights (land, IP, assets). Weak property-rights-related regulations should be flagged as ACMDs because they reduce investment, innovation, and productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Domestic competition as an evaluation pillar
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic Competition: A competitive domestic market fosters innovation, efficiency, and consumer benefits. The ACMD model measures how government policies either enhance or restrict firm-level competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a regulation limits the number/range of suppliers, restricts market entry, confers favoritism or protections to incumbents, or otherwise dampens incentives to compete. Balance this against regulations that legitimately address market failures (e.g., monopolistic behavior, environmental harms).

rubrics_metrics.name: International competition as an evaluation pillar
rubrics_metrics.description: International Competition: Evaluates a country’s openness to trade and foreign investment. Policies that impose tariffs, restrict financial flows, or hinder market access limit economic efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess regulations for trade-restrictive effects, barriers to foreign entrants, or distortions that disadvantage international competition. Consider interaction effects between domestic and international competition pillars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic-growth impact / GDP-per-capita prioritization metric
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic Growth: Productivity and GDP growth suffer under ACMDs; distortions remove pressures that drive innovation and efficiency. Improvements to domestic competition (i.e., elimination of anticompetitive regulation) have a three to four times greater impact on GDP per capita than similar border trade openings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use estimated GDP-per-capita impacts as a prioritization metric when deciding which anticompetitive regulations to target for repeal or modification. Quantify expected economic gains from removing specific regulatory distortions where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition and market health indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Competition and Market Health: ACMDs erode healthy competition, leading to higher prices, lower quality, less choice, complacent incumbents, oligopolistic or monopolistic markets, and associated corruption and rent-seeking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess regulations by their effects on prices, quality, consumer choice, innovation incentives, market concentration, and potential for rent-seeking/corruption. Indicators of diminished market health should flag regulations for remedial action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typology of Anti-Competitive Market Distortions (ACMDs)
rubrics_metrics.description: A typology of ACMDs offers a useful starting point for identifying harmful types of regulation (see referenced typology and literature).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use an established typology to classify regulatory distortions (e.g., licensing burdens, operational requirements, tariffs, favoritism). Typology aids systematic screening and comparison across sectors and regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of international and national case studies and OECD country reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: The Toolkit has been used by countries (Canada, South Korea, Mexico, Brazil, Greece, Iceland, Portugal, Romania, Tunisia, ASEAN countries) and in sectoral reviews (e.g., Tunisia tourism) to identify burdens like licensing and operational requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage OECD reports and country case studies as empirical evidence and implementation examples. Case studies provide concrete examples of burdens and remedies that can inform U.S. agency adaptations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult experts and adapt Toolkit to agency-specific needs
rubrics_metrics.description: The FTC and DOJ may benefit from consulting scholars with expertise using the Toolkit (e.g., Sean Ennis) and tailoring Toolkit analysis to meet needs of particular federal agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage external experts and experienced practitioners when developing agency guidance. Where necessary, adjust screening thresholds, technical assumptions, and operational steps to reflect statutory mandates, sectoral differences, and agency missions while preserving transparent competition-focused criteria.
